hens_rule_text: up to 5 chickens allowed on lots of 6,000 sq ft or less; 1 more chicken per additional 1,000 sq ft on larger lots; no roosters
permit_notes: The city's zoning self-help page does not describe a chicken-keeping permit process, only zoning setback standards; a separate coop building permit may apply depending on structure size, unconfirmed.
setback_notes: Structures for keeping animals must meet the zoning district's setbacks and be at least 10 ft from any lot line; one search extract also described uncovered enclosures needing 75 ft from residences, but this was not confirmed against the primary text.
coop_rules: Enclosure size scales with the number of birds (1,000 sq ft of lot per bird beyond the first 5 on a 6,000 sq ft lot); noisy fowl such as roosters, turkeys, guinea fowl, peacocks and geese are banned outright.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Anchorage Municipal Code Title 21 (Land Use Planning), Sec. 21.05.070.D, animal-keeping standards; noise and animal-care rules also sit in Title 17 (Animals), enforced by Animal Care and Control.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: The city's own zoning self-help page for animals (muni.org) directly states the 5-chicken/6,000 sq ft baseline, the 1,000 sq ft per additional bird formula, the 10 ft lot-line setback and the ban on noisy fowl including roosters; a secondary search extract citing a 75 ft residence setback for uncovered enclosures could not be reconciled with the official page.
